title: Juan Rulfo publica su obra monumental Pedro Páramo.
text: Juan Nepomuceno Carlos Pérez Rulfo Vizcaíno​ fue un escritor, guionista y fotógrafo mexicano, perteneciente a la Generación del 52.​​ Es considerado uno de los escritores hispanoamericanos más importantes del siglo XX.​​​ Su reputación se asienta en dos de sus tres obras narrativas: el libro de cuentos El Llano en llamas, publicado en 1953, y su novela Pedro Páramo, publicada en 1955.​​ En sus obras se presenta un…

title: The organization known as El Yunque was allegedly formed in this year.
text: The Organización Nacional del Yunque or simply El Yunque (in English: The Anvil) is the name of an alleged Mexican secret society whose existence was first claimed by journalist Alvaro Delgado in 2003.

title: The Querétaro Intercontinental Airport is established.
text: Querétaro Intercontinental Airport (IATA: QRO, ICAO: MMQT) is an international airport located in the municipalities of Colón and El Marqués, Querétaro, Mexico. It handles the national and international air traffic of the Querétaro Metropolitan area and can function as an alternate airport to Mexico City International Airport.

title: 1955 Mexican legislative election.
text: Legislative elections were held in Mexico on 4 July 1955. They were first federal elections in which women were able to vote after President Adolfo Ruiz Cortines introduced unrestricted citizenship for women on 17 October 1953, meeting one of his main campaign promises.

title: September 10–20: Hurricane Hilda (1955).
text: Hurricane Hilda was a strong Category 3 hurricane that was the second in a succession of three hurricanes to strike near Tampico, Mexico. The eighth named storm of the 1955 Atlantic hurricane season, Hilda formed from a tropical wave on September 10 near the Lesser Antilles.

title: Club de Yates de Acapulco opens its doors.
text: Club de Yates de Acapulco is a yacht club located in Acapulco, Mexico. Opened in December 1955, it served as host of the sailing events for the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City.

title: The 1955 Pan American Games take place in Mexico City.
text: The 1955 Pan American Games, officially known as II Pan American Games and commonly known as Mexico 1955 (Spanish: México 1955), opened on March 12, 1955, at University Stadium in Mexico City, Mexico, in front of a capacity crowd of 100,000 spectators. A total of 2,583 athletes from 22 nations marched in review and formed ranks upon the infield.

title: The Tigres del México win the Mexican League.
text: The Tigres de Quintana Roo are a professional baseball team in the Mexican League based in Cancún, Quintana Roo, Mexico. The team is part of the Southern Division (Zona Sur).
